description: Epic auto-start: autonomous progression of linked issues on terminal events, with idle/running/paused state machine, CLI/API/Web lifecycle actions, and active→idle migration.

tasks.title: Epic state machine: rename Active→Idle, add Running, with Start/Pause/Resume + idempotency and schema migration
tasks.description: Update EpicStatus enum to Idle/Running/Paused/Done/Closed (rename Active→Idle, add Running). Rework Epic.Transitions.cs: Create→Idle; new Start() (Idle→Running); Pause() restricted to Running (reject from Idle); Resume() targets Running (not Active); MarkDone valid from Idle/Running. Make Start/Pause/Resume no-ops when already in target state (idempotent at grain boundary; domain stays strict). Add EF Core migration backfilling Epics.Status 'active'→'idle', with legacy 'active' parsing defensively mapped to Idle.
acceptanceCriteria: EpicStatus enum has Idle, Running, Paused, Done, Closed; Active is removed.
Epic.Create yields Idle; Start transitions Idle→Running; Pause only succeeds from Running (throws from Idle); Resume transitions Paused→Running.
Start on an already-Running epic, Pause on an already-Paused epic, and Resume on an already-Running epic are no-ops (no exception, no event recorded).
MarkDone succeeds from Idle and Running; throws EpicPausedCannotMarkDoneException from Paused (unchanged).
Close from any non-terminal state transitions to Closed (unchanged).
EF migration updates existing Epics.Status='active' rows to 'idle'; migration up/down tested.
StatusName/ParseStatus round-trip Idle/Running/Paused/Done/Closed; legacy 'active' parses to Idle.
EpicLifecycleSpecs / EpicTransitionsSpecs cover all new transitions, idempotency, and rejection cases; existing transition tests updated and green.
tasks.output: packages/server/src/Mohist.Server/Epic/Domain/EpicStatus.cs, Epic.Transitions.cs; EF migration under Infrastructure/Data; updated domain specs
tasks.notes: All downstream tasks depend on the new enum + transition surface. Keep the domain strict (throw on invalid); idempotency is enforced by grain-level try/catch in T-002.

tasks.title: EpicGrain autonomous progression: StartAsync, ReconcileAfterTerminalAsync, TryStartNext (shared SelectStartableNext)
tasks.spec: specs/epic-lifecycle/spec.md#Autonomous advancement on terminal issue events
tasks.description: Add EpicGrain.StartAsync (Idle→Running + TryStartNext), ReconcileAfterTerminalAsync (supersedes AutoMarkDoneIfReadyAsync: skip if paused/terminal; MarkDone if ready; else TryStartNext when Running, no-op when Idle), and TryStartNext (return if any linked in_progress; pick next via EpicProgress.SelectStartableNext; call IIssueGrain.StartWorkAsync; swallow+log start failures leaving epic running-but-idle). Update ResumeAsync to call ReconcileAfterTerminalAsync. Factor EpicProgress.SelectStartableNext from private to shared internal so read-model and grain use identical ordering. Enforce idempotency at the grain boundary (catch domain throws for already-target-state and return current DTO).
acceptanceCriteria: EpicGrain.StartAsync transitions Idle→Running and starts the first startable linked issue; if none startable, epic is Running with no error.
ReconcileAfterTerminalAsync is a no-op for Paused/Done/Closed; marks Done when readiness satisfied; calls TryStartNext only when Running; does NOT advance when Idle.
TryStartNext returns without starting when a linked issue is in_progress (serial slot occupied); selects the highest-priority CanStart/no-StartBlocker issue otherwise; excludes cancelled issues.
TryStartNext swallows and logs exceptions from IIssueGrain.StartWorkAsync, leaving the epic Running (nextIssueReason still computed by the read model).
ResumeAsync re-evaluates: auto-done if ready, else TryStartNext when Running.
StartAsync/PauseAsync/ResumeAsync are idempotent at the grain boundary (no error returned for already-target-state).
EpicProgress.SelectStartableNext is reusable (no longer private) and shared by both the grain and the read-model; cancel-skip + priority ordering identical.

EpicAutoDoneSpecs / new EpicProgression grain specs cover start, reconcile-on-done, reconcile-on-cancel (in-progress cancelled → next advances), failed-issue-holds-epic, running-but-idle, and idempotency.
tasks.notes: Race safety is structural: Pause + reconcile are both grain methods on EpicGrain, serialized by Orleans turn-based execution. IIssueGrain.StartWorkAsync may need WorkflowProjectContext — confirm during impl (see design Open Question Q2).

tasks.title: Event wiring: subscribe EpicAutoDoneHandler to both terminal events; generalize reconciliation sweep
tasks.description: Generalize EpicAutoDoneHandler to subscribe to both com.mohist.issue.work-completed and com.mohist.issue.closed, dispatching both to EpicGrain.ReconcileAfterTerminalAsync. Generalize EpicReconciliationService sweep to call ReconcileAfterTerminalAsync on Running (and Idle for auto-done) candidates so missed events recover.
acceptanceCriteria: EpicAutoDoneHandler subscribes to both com.mohist.issue.work-completed and com.mohist.issue.closed and calls ReconcileAfterTerminalAsync for each (with projectid/issueid extension parsing reused).
A cancelled in-progress linked issue (IssueClosed event) triggers reconcile that advances the next startable issue.
A done linked issue (IssueWorkCompleted event) triggers reconcile as before.
Duplicate/out-of-order terminal signals converge to the correct epic state (no double-advance, no double-transition).
EpicReconciliationService sweep invokes ReconcileAfterTerminalAsync (not the old AutoMarkDoneIfReadyAsync) and includes Running epics in its candidate set.
EpicAutoDoneHandlerSpecs / EpicReconciliationServiceSpecs cover both events, the cancelled-in-progress advancement path, and duplicate-signal idempotency.
tasks.notes: Both terminal events must trigger reconcile because both clear the serial in-progress slot; missing the closed subscription deadlocks the epic on cancel.

tasks.title: HTTP API: POST /epics/{id}/start; update pause/resume semantics and error codes
tasks.description: Add POST /api/projects/{projectRef}/epics/{id}/start route calling EpicGrain.StartAsync. Update PauseRouteAsync/ResumeRouteAsync to surface the new semantics: Pause requires Running (map a new EpicNotRunningException → 409 EPIC_NOT_RUNNING); Resume targets Running. Keep EpicAlreadyTerminalException → 409. Resume/Start return the resulting EpicDto.
acceptanceCriteria: POST /epics/{id}/start transitions an idle epic to running and returns EpicDto with status 'running'.
POST /epics/{id}/pause on a running epic returns 200 with status 'paused'; on an idle epic returns 409 EPIC_NOT_RUNNING.
POST /epics/{id}/resume on a paused epic returns 200 with status 'running'.
Start/Pause/Resume on an epic already in the target state return 200 (idempotent), not an error.
Start/Pause/Resume on a terminal (done/closed) epic return 409 EPIC_ALREADY_TERMINAL.
EpicRoutes integration tests cover start, pause (running + idle-rejected), resume, idempotency, and terminal rejection.
tasks.notes: Start is the only genuinely new endpoint; pause/resume routes already exist and only need semantic/error-code updates.

tasks.title: CLI: mo epic start command; status display for idle/running
tasks.description: Add `mo epic start {id|number}` subcommand mirroring existing pause/resume/done commands (project-ref option, output option, POST to /epics/{id}/start). Update CLI epic status display strings to render 'idle' and 'running'. Confirm Workflow-core CLI gains no issue/epic dependency.
acceptanceCriteria: `mo epic start {n}` on an idle epic transitions it to running and prints the resulting epic state.
Start accepts both epic id and epic number, and honors --project/-p and -o output options like other epic commands.
CLI status display renders 'idle' and 'running' correctly in table/json output.
Start against a terminal epic surfaces the API error (409) to the user cleanly.
CliEpicCommandSpecs cover start success, start by number, output formatting, and error surfacing.

tasks.title: Web UI: epic lifecycle header actions, useStartEpic, demote Next Issue card to info-only
tasks.description: Extend entities/epic EpicStatus enum with Idle/Running (rename Active→Idle). Add useStartEpic mutation (POST .../start) with query invalidation. Make the EpicDetailPage header state-driven: idle shows 'Start Epic' primary action, running shows 'Pause', paused shows 'Resume', done/closed show none. Remove the epic-detail-next-start button block from the Next Issue card (keep the next-issue identity + next-issue-reason). Retain per-row linked-issue-start. Start Epic/Pause/Resume refresh epic state and dashboard on success.
acceptanceCriteria: EpicStatus enum in entities/epic includes Idle and Running; legacy 'active' is treated as Idle.
useStartEpic calls POST /epics/{id}/start and invalidates the epic query on success.
EpicDetailPage header renders 'Start Epic' (primary) when idle, 'Pause' when running, 'Resume' when paused, and no lifecycle action when done/closed.
The Next Issue card no longer renders the epic-detail-next-start button; it still shows the next issue and next-issue-reason.
Per-row linked-issue-start is still rendered for individually startable issues and does not transition the epic to running.
Invoking Start Epic/Pause/Refresh refreshes the epic status and dashboard (progress, nextIssueReason) on success.
EpicDetailPage tests cover all four header states, removal of epic-detail-next-start, retained linked-issue-start, and successful mutation → refresh.
tasks.notes: Rename Active→Idle in the web enum will require updating existing references (e.g. markDoneBlocked check at EpicDetailPage.tsx:447).
